lines: illusion n.
/ɪˈluː.ʒən/
▪an idea or opinion that is wrong, especially about yourself
错误的观念;幻想; 错觉
▪under the illusion that+句子 有...的错觉
1 We need to accept the fact that people
bought these houses under the illusion that
their value would just keep on rising. L36 N2L79
2 Needless to say, she was under the illusion
that he was honest until he was caught stealing
some money. L36
3 It’s possible that she's under the illusion that
she'll get the job. L38

pastoral adj.  idyllic adj.
/ˈpɑːstərəl/ /ɪˈdɪlɪk/
田园的               田园诗般的
1 The painting depicts an idyllic pastoral scene
of shepherds watching over their sheep.
2 We can make the assumptions that an idyllic
pastoral life involves fresh air and the beauty
of nature. L38
3 The painter captured idyllic pastoral life in a
masterpiece, depicting a stretch of land with a
small house among the hills. L39
breed - bred v.
/bri ːd/ /bred/
▪if a place, situation, or thing breeds a particular type of
person, it produces that type
养育,哺育,生养〔某一类型的人〕
▪born and bred: born and having grown up in a particular
place and having the typical qualities of someone from
that place 土生土长
1 It has never been explained why they were
born and bred in another country. L40
2 There is a chance in a million that they were
actually born and bred in the same
environment. L36
3 Evidence suggests that he was born and
bred in London. L36
rapture n.
/ˈræptʃə/
1 go into raptures 狂喜
2 She went into raptures about the climate,
the food and the spring flowers when taking
a stroll in the pastoral countryside. L23
3 After overcoming all sorts of obstacles, she
went into raptures at the news of her success.
extol v.
/ɪkˈstəʊl/
▪to praise something very much 赞美,颂扬
▪extol the virtues/benefits of something
1 Educators should extol the virtues of making
mistakes and encourage children to try more. L35
2 It has long been known that doctors extol the
virtues of eating less fat. L38
3 In the speech, he extolled the benefits of
filling cities with trees. L28
superior adj.
/suːˈpɪəriə/
▪ better, more powerful, more effective etc than a similar
person or thing, especially one that you are competing
against 更好的;更强的;更有效的,优越的
▪be superior to ... 优于;胜于
1 He explained that he is indeed rich, since his
income is superior to his expenses, and his
expense is equal to his wishes. L19&L2
2 A closed mind is when you believe that your
way of making a profit is superior to everyone
else’s. N2L80
3 The manager pointed out that his products
were far superior to others. N2L58
cockcrow n.
/ˈkɒk.kr əʊ/
▪the time in the early morning when the sun rises
黎明,鸡鸣时分
▪ the sound of a cock (=a male chicken) crowing
(= making a sound): 鸡叫
1 I was woken up with a start by the sudden
cockcrow. L2
2 As soon as they heard the first cockcrow, they
quickly got back to the box as if they had never
left. L28
3 I am accustomed to getting up as soon as I
hear the first cockcrow. N2L94

twitter v.
/ˈtwɪtə/
1 if a bird twitters, it makes a lot of short high sounds
〔⻦〕鸣啭, 啾啾叫,吱吱叫

twitter every morning in the trees near my house

starts to depict pictures on the wall. L38

in the spring, birds twitter. N2L77
glint v.
/ɡlɪnt/
▪ if a shiny surface glints, it gives out small flashes of light
闪烁,闪光
1 What a relief it was when we found his gold
ring which was glinting in the sunlight. L39
2 I found it hard to tell who he was because of
the sun glinting on his glasses. L29
3 It was not until she saw something glinting on
the carpet that she realized the diamond wasn’t
lost. N2L35 L21
pasture n.
/ˈpɑːstʃə/
▪land or a field that is covered with grass and is used for
cattle, sheep etc to feed on 牧场
1 He was anxious to take the horses out to the
pasture. L22
2 With the passage of time, the deserted village
became surrounded by fields and pasture land. L38
3 It seems that this pasture can no longer carry
such a large number of cattle and sheep. L9&L18
virtually adv.
/ˈvɜːtʃuəli/
1 almost 实际上,几乎,差不多
2 Virtually everyone knows that great minds
think alike. L21
3 It’s virtually impossible to...
4 It’s virtually impossible to get advance information
without any efforts.  L40
5 It’s virtually impossible to be exempted from
military service when going to high school. L11
dubious adj.
/ˈdjuː.biəs/
be dubious about
1 probably not honest, true, right etc 可疑的,靠不住的
2 I am a little dubious about what he said of
being granted permission to the temple. L40
3 I hope you don't mind the interference, but he
has been associated with some dubious
characters. L35&L23
4 I presume that the results of this policy will
remain dubious for some time. L36
privilege n.
/ˈprɪvɪlɪdʒ/
▪special advantage that is given only to one person or
group of people 特权,特殊 待遇
▪the privilege of doing something have the privilege of
doing sth. L4
1 He announced that he had been given the
privilege of meeting the queen. L39
2 From the look on her face, I can deduce that
she hopes to have the privilege of working with
them again. L38
3 They are naive enough to believe that they will
be granted the privilege of coming to the
palace again. L36
misery n.
/ˈmɪzəri/
1 great suffering that is caused for example by
being very poor or very sick 痛苦,困苦,苦难
2 You don’t strike me as the kind of person who
lived in misery for years. L37
3 She is not in the least grateful for your help, as
all that money brought nothing but sadness and
misery. L39&L40
4 Everything conspired to make her life a misery.

party, I had little desire to make his acquaintance.

treat n.
/triːt/
1 as a special treat...作为一种特殊的款待

as a special treat. L40
3 We took the kids to the zoo as a special treat.
did/who/why/where/when...

to stay over at a school-friend’s. L40
dweller n.
/ˈdwel ə/
1 a person or animal that lives in a particular place
居住在城里/ 镇上/洞穴中等的人[动物]
2 He poured scorn on idea that both city and
town dwellers should pay the same tax. L36
3 There is no doubt that city dwellers have a
higher death rate than country people do. L25
4 He pretended to be an urban dweller. L40
stagger v.
/ˈstæɡə/
1 to walk or move unsteadily, almost falling over
蹒跚; 摇摇晃晃地走
2 He staggered home with great difficulty. L25
3 After he was attacked, he managed to stagger
to the phone and call for help. N2L67
4 However painful it was, I managed to stagger
the last few steps. L35
exotic adj.
/ɪɡˈzɒtɪk/
▪something that is exotic seems unusual and interesting
because it is related to a foreign country – use this to show
approval 异国风情的,外国情调的〔含褒义〕
1 She dreamed of flying to an exotic place. N2L38
2 She seems perturbed by the exotic clothes on
the floor. L39
3 His ideas shed light on why exotic foods are
available in supermarkets. L38
4 He obtained the money to go on all these
exotic journeys by deception. L40
glow n.
/ɡləʊ/
1 a soft steady light 光亮;光辉
2 With the glow from the lamp, it’s easy to read
the words engraved on the wall. L38
3 Only when the lamplight gave a warm glow to
the room did he realized that +句子 L40
4 The candles shed a soft glow on her face, which
captured the attention of all the men in the room.
descend v.
/dɪˈsend/
▪if darkness, silence, a feeling etc descends, it becomes
dark etc or you start to feel something, especially suddenly
〔黑暗、寂静等突然〕降临;〔感 情等突然〕袭来,来临
▪ descend on/upon/over
1 After she tore up the letter, total silence
descended on the room... L40
2 Something frightening was about to descend
on him. L24
3 I can’t help noticing that as he entered, a silence
descended over the gathered audience. L37

41 Grammar
be always/forever老是/总是 doing sth. L2
He never does his homework on time and is forever
getting into trouble at school.
save v. 省去(诸多不便;痛苦;悲惨;穷困)
▪If you lent me £5, it would save me a trip to the bank.
[save sb. sth.]
▪If you phone for an appointment, it'll save you waiting.
[save sb. doing sth.]
▪I’ll get a taxi from the station to save you the trouble of
coming to collect me. [save sb. the trouble/bother (of
doing sth.)]
定语从句:用that引导,不用which/who
▪【考试VS日常生活】被定从修饰的词前有adj.est,
[first, last, any, only few, little, much, no , some, very].
▪This is the best TV set that is made in China.
▪It is the fastest sports car that has ever been made.
▪He is the smartest person that I know.
something comforting:adj. 后置
▪something/somebody/anything/anybody
▪There is nothing wrong with the watch.
▪There's someone interesting at the party.
▪Do you have something delicious to eat?
▪Is there anybody available to answer the phone?
Nor 句首 + 倒装
▪Nor have I seen him since that day.
▪Nor did she want to go to the party.
▪Nor did they have any idea how to solve the problem.
▪Nor should you underestimate the importance of this
decision.

tolerate... for
▪It is naive to believe she can tolerate
criticism for the benefit of personal
growth. L36
▪ I suspect that he won’t be able to
tolerate long hours of work for the
dubious benefit of achieving his career
goals. L30

can tolerate inconvenience for the
privilege of living in a big house. L36
beyond me
▪not something that I can understand
▪It's beyond me why he made a horrible
hoax call to his girlfriend on the wedding
day. L40
▪It’s beyond me why you failed to connect
the dots. N2L16 L38
▪Why he seemed perturbed by the
name was beyond me. L39
▪How she got large sums of money was
beyond me. L14
do without
▪to live or do something without a particular thing
没有...也能应付 没有......也行
▪We ran out of milk, but we can do
without it until we go grocery shopping.
▪It is clear that she cannot do without a
computer while working. L21
▪During the camping trip, we realized
we could do without electricity and still
have a great time.
travel miles to do sth.
▪My mother reprimanded me for traveling
miles just to eat a bowl of dumplings. L31
▪We were willing to travel miles to see
the breathtaking sunset at the beach. L4
▪The mere fact [that she would travel
miles to visit you during the holidays]
means she likes you. L34
be available for
▪Unable to find his preferred
ingredients, the chef had to make do
with what was available for the dinner.
▪I was wondering if there a room available
for you tonight. N2L68
▪There is a considerable number of books
available for you to choose from. L19
come up to
▪come up to somewhere:to come from one place
to another, especially from the south of a country
to the north or from a smaller place to a larger one.
▪come up to someone: to move towards someone
▪He came up to the front of the meeting
room and presented the contract in
black and white. L37
▪It’s true that he came up to the house
that evening, armed with a music box
and a pot of tea. L16 N2L55
▪She came up to me and acquainted
me with what truly happened that
night. L36
draw to a close
▪The festival drew to a close with the
fantastic fireworks that lit up the night
sky. L11
▪ What invariably happens is that as the
semester drew to a close, students
began making great efforts to prepare
for their final exams. L33 N2L78
make do with
▪to use what is available although it is not enough
or what you wanted
▪She had to make do with the old
computer.
▪We ran out of milk, so we had to make
do with black coffee for breakfast. N2L88
▪As the accident brought the traffic to a
grinding halt, I had to make do with the
subway. L39
run wild
▪If someone, often a child, runs wild, that person
behaves as they want to without being controlled
by anyone.
失控,天马行空,随心所欲
▪After being kept in the house all day,
the children were allowed to run wild in
the backyard. N2L10
▪The imagination of the author seemed
to run wild, creating fascinating worlds
in each novel. L27
▪They insist that all parents not let their
children run wild. L22
Few things could be more impressive
than....
▪Few things could be more impressive
than seeing the mountain view while
the curtain goes up. L22
▪Few things could be more impressive
than the beauty of the ocean that
consists of a bewildering variety of sea
life. L13 N2L90
